core_obligations: For a pair of morphisms from schemes into the space, show that their fibre product over the space is an algebraic space: choose the presentation, observe that the base changes of the members of the presentation give a jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms with sources that are schemes, and apply the bootstrap theorem (proof lines 2673-2690).

Show that the morphism from that fibre product to the fibre product of the two schemes over the base is a monomorphism, and that it is locally quasi-finite by checking after the etale family, where it becomes a composition of a closed immersion and an etale morphism (proof lines 2691-2705).
Conclude that the fibre product is a scheme, using that it is a locally quasi-finite separated algebraic space over a scheme, and hence that the diagonal is representable (proof lines 2706-2695).

Deduce that the diagonal is a monomorphism and locally quasi-finite, and then, by checking the corresponding properties of the representable transformation on schemes, that it is separated and locally of finite type (proof lines 2697-2712).
proof_roadmap: Representability: fibre products of schemes over the space are algebraic spaces (proof lines 2673-2690).
Monomorphism and local quasi-finiteness of the comparison morphism (proof lines 2691-2705).
From algebraic space to scheme, giving representability of the diagonal (proof lines 2706-2695).
Transfer of the remaining properties (proof lines 2697-2712).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts five properties of the diagonal of a formal algebraic space over a scheme: representability, monomorphism, local quasi-finiteness, local finite typeness and separatedness (statement lines 2666-2671). The proof produces the first by testing against a pair of morphisms from schemes: for such a pair the fibre product is a sheaf, and applying the presentation of the space and base changing gives a jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms from schemes onto that fibre product, so the fibre product is an algebraic space by the bootstrap theorem (proof lines 2673-2690). The same computation shows that the morphism from that fibre product to the fibre product of the two schemes over the base is a monomorphism, and that it is locally quasi-finite because after precomposing with the family it becomes a composition of a closed immersion and an etale morphism; a proposition on locally quasi-finite separated algebraic spaces then makes the fibre product a scheme, which is representability of the diagonal (proof lines 2683-2695). The remaining four properties are then deduced from that: the same computation shows the diagonal is a monomorphism and locally quasi-finite, and the principle allowing properties of representable transformations to be checked on schemes identifies the diagonal with a monomorphism of schemes, hence separated, and with a locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes, hence locally of finite type (proof lines 2697-2712). The claim is H2: the first part is a genuine argument with a base-change family and a reduction from algebraic spaces to schemes, and the rest is a two-step transfer, with each step named rather than assumed.
